title: What If the Banana Disappeared? It Has Happened Before

scenes.text: What if the banana disappeared? It already did once. The one you eat today is the replacement.
Until the 1960s the banana on store shelves was the Gros Michel. A soil fungus destroyed it.
Growers switched to the Cavendish, which resisted that fungus. Today it makes up about 97 percent of banana exports.
Now a new strain of the same fungus, Tropical Race 4, is killing Cavendish farms across Asia, Africa and Latin America.
Its spores can stay in soil for decades, and nobody has found a way to wipe them out.
Almost every Cavendish is a genetic copy of the others, which is why one disease can threaten them all.

description:
What if the banana disappeared?
It has happened before: a fungus wiped out the Gros Michel, and a new strain now threatens the Cavendish that replaced it.
